decision_table.name: Determine_MT_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Montana state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in MT (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
MT filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in MT if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in MT - Employees working in MT - Tangible personal property located in MT - Real property located in MT
Reference: Montana Code Annotated § 15-30-2101 (Apportionment and allocation) Reference: Montana Department of Revenue Nexus Guidance

actions.action: // Economic nexus established per Wayfair - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
MT filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
Economic nexus threshold: $100,000 gross receipts OR 200 transactions in MT.
Following South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), MT requires filing if a corporation exceeds economic nexus thresholds, even without physical presence.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: Montana Department of Revenue Economic Nexus Guidance

No MT nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or economic nexus thresholds. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: Montana Code Annotated § 15-30-2101 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_MT_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate MT state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income. Montana starts with federal taxable income and applies state modifications.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
MT state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
Montana uses federal taxable income (excluding IRC 199A qualified business income deduction) as the starting point for state tax calculation.
MT ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to MT) - State income tax refunds received during the year - IRC Section 199A qualified business income deduction (if taken federally) - Expenses related to exempt income - Certain federal deductions not allowed by Montana
MT SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on MT state and municipal bonds - State income taxes paid - Montana net operating loss deduction (subject to MT limitations)
Reference: Montana Form CIT Schedule I (Additions to Federal Taxable Income) Reference: Montana Form CIT Schedule II (Subtractions from Federal Taxable Income) Reference: Montana Code Annotated § 15-30-2120 (Adjustments to federal taxable income)

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have MT nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_MT_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate MT state corporate income tax. Applies MT 6.75% flat rate (or 7.0% for water's edge election) to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
MT state corporate income tax calculation (standard 6.75% rate):
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to MT: × [MT apportionment percentage] 3. MT additions: + [Federal interest, state tax refunds, IRC 199A addback, etc.] 4. MT subtractions: - [MT municipal interest, state taxes paid, MT NOL, etc.] 5. MT taxable income: = [Result] 6. MT tax rate: × 6.75% (standard flat rate) 7. MT income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. MT credits: - [Jobs, research, energy, infrastructure, etc.] 9. MT tax liability: = [Final tax]
MT uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
MT tax rate: 6.75% flat rate (standard)
MT provides various tax credits including: - Jobs creation tax credit - Research and development credit - Energy production credit - Infrastructure investment credit - Alternative energy investment credit
Reference: Montana Form CIT (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Montana Code Annotated § 15-30-2101 (Tax rate of 6.75%) Reference: Montana Code Annotated § 15-30-2110 (Single-sales apportionment)

MT state corporate income tax calculation (7.0% rate for water's edge election):
Corporations that make a water's edge election pay a slightly higher rate of 7.0% instead of the standard 6.75% rate.
The water's edge election limits the income reported to U.S. operations and specific international operations, simplifying compliance for multinational corporations.
All other calculation steps are identical to the standard rate calculation.
Reference: Montana Form CIT (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Montana Code Annotated § 15-30-2101 (Tax rate of 7.0% for water's edge)

No MT nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in MT. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: Montana Code Annotated § 15-30-2101 (Nexus requirements)

No MT taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has MT nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
MT net operating loss (NOL) rules: - MT NOL is computed under IRC Section 172 with MT modifications - NOL carryforward allowed (subject to MT limitations) - NOL deduction may be limited similar to federal rules
Reference: Montana Form CIT (Corporation Income Tax Return) Reference: Montana Code Annotated § 15-30-2120 (MT NOL provisions)
